These two kinds of statements are not equally expensive. An essay costs nothing to publish. A rate increase is a wager with revenue attached: it only works if customers stay. The rate card is the stronger claim about the world, and Nebius has been making that claim in steadily more binding forms. Its first Blackwell capacity auction cleared 15% above prior pricing, and chief executive Arkady Volozh says Nebius could "sell today our entire 2027 capacity" but is holding it for shorter deals at $40–50 million per megawatt 7.

...

The bill lands on everyone renting by the hour. The other side of the wager is Nebius's own balance sheet: liabilities of $17.6 billion, 2026 capex guided at $20–25 billion, and three customers making up 24%, 21% and 14% of revenue 7. Behind them sit the lenders. July's $775 million facility↗ (led by MUFG, priced at SOFR plus 2.50%, maturing in 2030, secured on deployed GPUs and contracted cash flows, with covenants tied to debt-service coverage) is explicitly a template Nebius wants to repeat across more than $40 billion of contracted revenue with Microsoft▼−0.28% — Microsoft, down 0.28 percent today and Meta 8. Rising spot prices flowing into longer contracts is also, as Morningstar noted, what turns this build-out profitable through 2027 1.

...

If bookings hold at the new card, scarcity is confirmed and asset-backed finance gets cheaper to roll forward. If they flinch, the slowdown chorus gets its data point and the risk shifts from customers to lenders. One warning light I could not check: bears cite secondhand accelerator prices as the earliest signal of capex trouble, and no published index I could reach this week carries that number: the organized market for used GPUs↗ itself only opened on 17 July 10. That leaves the rate card as the cleanest public signal available.

When essays and price lists disagree, believe the price list, then verify it. Three markers after 1 October: on-demand utilization at the new rates, whether the next capacity auction again clears above the last, and whether Nebius funds its 2027 build from customer prepayments rather than another equity raise 7. The labs asked for time. The market is about to learn what an hour of it costs.

results.title: Making AI Work: Nebius Increases AI Cloud Pricing as Demand for Computing Power Surges, ETEnterpriseai
highlights:
On-demand rates for some central processing units, made by AMD and Intel, and memory offerings have also been hiked.

Cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected Nvidia chips from October 1, marking the company's second price hike in three months. Demand for computing capacity to train and run AI models is surging; rival CoreWeave said earlier in the day that it is signing contracts at higher prices. Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between 17 per cent and 21 per cent. On-demand rates for some central processing units, made by AMD and Intel, and memory offerings have also been hiked. 

Prices of some CPU-only instances will rise by 25 per cent and those of memory offerings by about 41 per cent, the company said. The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm said that customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive commitment discounts. Nebius' price increases follow a quarter of rapid growth in its AI cloud business, as the company signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each. Neocloud firms like Nebius rent out high-powered chips and data centre infrastructure needed for AI models.

results.title: 英伟达“干儿子”带头涨价！GPU租金全线上调 最高涨21%：H100老卡也涨17%_腾讯新闻
highlights:
快科技9月18日消息，据报道，荷兰 AI算力租赁商 Nebius宣布，自2026年10月1日起全面上调按需GPU算力价格。英伟达 H100、H200、B200和B300的租金涨幅分别达17%、20%、19%和21%。

其中B300从7.85美元/小时（约合人民币52.67元/小时） 涨至9.50美元/小时（约合人民币63.75元/小时）。

值得一提的是，Nebius的涨价覆盖全系GPU，连2022年发布的H100也涨了17%。旧卡租金不降反升，直接反驳了“GPU两三年就报废”的折旧质疑。

AI怀疑论者曾认为云厂商6年折旧年限高估了芯片长期价值，Nebius此举意味着H100在服役约4年后仍有强劲的商业价值。

这已是Nebius数月内第二次提价。今年5月该公司已对按需容量平均提价29%，对可抢占容量提价51%。此外， AMD EPYC Genoa CPU价格将上涨25%，内存服务价格将上涨约41%。

Nebius涨价的底气来自实打实的业绩。2026年第二季度营收达5.82亿美元，同比增长454%，超出市场预期。

其AI云业务收入达5.75亿美元（约合人民币38.58亿元），同比增长514%。Nebius客户包括Meta和微软，英伟达今年7月披露持有其约9.3%股权，总计2226万股，是其重要的战略布局。

Nebius并非唯一涨价的业者。另一家获英伟达投资的 CoreWeave今年7月已全系提价约25%，并表示第三季度价格持续上升。两家头部算力租赁商同步提价，印证了AI算力需求仍远超供给，定价权正从叙事变成报表数字。

results.title: Nebius raises Nvidia GPU cloud prices 17–21% from October as AI compute demand surges | ServerRental
highlights:
Summary — Nebius, a cloud provider focused on AI infrastructure, has announced price increases of 17–21% for its Nvidia GPU cloud instances, effective October 2025. The company cited sustained and accelerating demand for AI compute capacity as the primary driver. The increases apply to on-demand GPU instances across multiple Nvidia accelerator generations, including H100 and H200 configurations, according to the company's published pricing updates.

The move follows a broader industry pattern of GPU cloud providers adjusting rates upward as data center capacity tightens and power availability becomes a limiting factor in key regions. For organizations renting GPU servers or evaluating AI Infrastructure options, the announcement signals that the cost curve for accelerated computing is not flattening as quickly as some procurement teams had projected.

## Key Facts of the Price Change

Nebius operates GPU clusters in Europe and North America, offering bare-metal and virtualized access to Nvidia accelerators. The announced changes affect:

- On-demand H100 GPU instances: approximately 17% price increase
- On-demand H200 GPU instances: approximately 19–21% price increase
- Reserved capacity contracts: reportedly subject to renegotiation based on term length and commitment volume

The company has not publicly disclosed exact per-hour rates for all configurations, but customers with active contracts received notifications with updated line items. According to the announcement, existing long-term reservations signed before a specific cutoff date will retain their original pricing until contract renewal.

...

### Budget Planning for AI Workloads

Teams with fixed AI infrastructure budgets should re-evaluate monthly burn rates. A 17–21% increase on GPU instances translates to meaningful additional spend for workloads that run continuously. For example, a training cluster consuming $50,000 per month in GPU compute would see costs rise by roughly $8,500–$10,500 monthly under the new rates.

### Renewed Interest in Bare-Metal and Dedicated Options

When cloud GPU prices rise, some teams shift workloads to Dedicated Servers with GPUs on monthly or quarterly contracts. Bare-metal GPU servers typically offer lower per-hour effective costs for sustained workloads because there is no virtualization overhead and pricing is fixed for the contract term. The trade-off is less elasticity: scaling down requires contract renegotiation or waiting for the term to expire.

...

Providers typically discount reserved instances by 30–50% compared to on-demand rates. As on-demand prices rise, the relative advantage of reservations grows. Teams with predictable training schedules should evaluate 1-year or 3-year reserved GPU capacity. However, reservation terms lock in specific hardware generations, which carries risk if newer accelerators become available mid-term.

...

### Consider Workload Duration

The economics of GPU rental differ sharply by workload duration:

- Short experiments (hours to days): On-demand cloud GPU instances remain the most practical option despite price increases. The flexibility to spin up and tear down quickly outweighs the per-hour premium.
- Medium training runs (weeks): Reserved instances or short-term bare-metal contracts often provide 30–40% savings over on-demand.
- Long-running training or inference (months): Dedicated Servers with GPU configurations or colocated hardware typically offer the lowest effective cost per GPU-hour, provided the team can manage the infrastructure.

...

According to the company's announcement, on-demand Nvidia GPU instance prices are increasing by 17–21% depending on the accelerator generation, effective October 2025.

Some CPU-only instances will become 25 per cent more expensive, while selected memory offerings will jump by about 41 per cent.

The increases come just three months after Nebius last fiddled with its prices, suggesting customers are still prepared to pay handsomely for scarce computing capacity.

...

Customers willing to reserve large-scale clusters for several months can avoid some of the impact. Nebius says commitment discounts are available for longer reservations, with its published pricing offering discounts of up to 35 per cent compared with on-demand rates.

The price rises follow a rapid quarter for Nebius’s AI cloud operation. The company signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each as demand for AI infrastructure continued to outrun available capacity.

results.title: AMD Warns Partners Of A 10% Price Hike On AI Chips ...
highlights:
## The Nebius Squeeze

The timing is not a coincidence. On the same day, Nebius, the AI cloud company that rents out Nvidia GPUs and AMD server chips, announced its own price hikes. Rental rates for AMD's EPYC Genoa CPUs are set to climb 25% starting October 1, according to reporting from Silicon UK and Proactive Investors. That's steeper than the 17% to 21% increase Nebius is applying to Nvidia GPU rentals, where H100 instances rise from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour and the newer B300 climbs from $7.85 to $9.50. Genoa memory prices are rising even faster, up 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour.

Put those two announcements together and you get a clean read on where AI infrastructure economics stand right now. Compute is still scarce. That's why a cloud provider can raise CPU rental prices faster than GPU rental prices and still expect customers to pay. Nebius shares rose as much as 11% on its own announcement, according to Yahoo Finance, and this marks the company's second round of AI cloud price hikes in a few months. TipRanks noted that cumulative increases on B300 instances now run close to 56% since earlier this year.
